card.name: Ballet
card.tagline: Italian Renaissance courts, perfected in France — turnout, line, and four centuries of perfectionism.
card.profile: Ballet (French: [balɛ]) is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the fifteenth century and later developed into a concert dance form in France and Russia. It has since become a widespread and highly technical form of dance with its own vocabulary. Ballet has been influential globally and has defined the foundational techniques which are used in many other dance genres and cultures. Various schools around the world have incorporated their own cultures. As a result, ballet has evolved in distinct ways.
card.insight: The first ballet was "Le Ballet Comique de la Reine," performed in Paris in 1581 at the wedding of Marguerite de Lorraine.

parts.note: The teacher introduces herself and the class.

steps.name: half-toe, full-toe
steps.description: A sequence of rising onto the balls of the feet and then the toes.

steps.name: pedals
steps.description: Alternating heel lifts while keeping the toes on the floor.

steps.name: elevés
steps.description: Rising onto the balls of the feet with both feet together.

steps.name: first position
steps.description: Feet in a V shape with heels together.

steps.name: second position
steps.description: Feet in an open V shape.

steps.name: fifth position
steps.description: One heel in front of the other toe.

lessons.teacher_style: The teacher is encouraging and emphasizes that ballet is accessible to everyone, regardless of their natural body type. She breaks down complex movements into simple, manageable steps, focusing on proper technique and body alignment.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teacher explicitly encourages students to work with their current physical limitations rather than striving for an idealized ballet body.
what_works: The teacher's clear, step-by-step instructions and her emphasis on not worrying about perfection make the lesson easy to follow.
what_hinders: The lack of varied camera angles might make it difficult to see the foot positions clearly.
